task.question: What position did Keir Starmer resign from on June 22, 2026 in the United Kingdom?
task.evidence: June 22 – Following months of criticism and pressure, Keir Starmer resigned as prime minister of the United Kingdom. Starmer later resigned his membership as Member of Parliament to assume his role as member of the Chiltern Hundreds on September 1.

Content: Sir Keir Starmer KCB KC (born 2 September 1962) is a British politician who has served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and Leader of the Labour Party since July 2024. He is the Member of Parliament (MP) for Holborn and St Pancras since 2015.
Keir Starmer was born on 2 September 1962 in Southwark, London. He was educated at Reigate Grammar School and studied law at the University of Leeds and St Edmund Hall, Oxford. He was called to the bar in 1987 and became a Queen's Counsel in 2002. He was Director of Public Prosecutions and Head of the Crown Prosecution Service from 2008 to 2013. He was knighted in 2014 for services to law and criminal justice.
Keir Starmer entered politics and was elected as the MP for Holborn and St Pancras in the 2015 general election. He served in Jeremy Corbyn's shadow cabinet as Shadow Brexit Secretary from 2016 to 2020. He was elected as Leader of the Labour Party in April 2020, succeeding Jeremy Corbyn. He became Leader of the Opposition in May 2020. He led Labour to victory in the 2024 United Kingdom general election and became Prime Minister on 5 July 2024.

Sir Keir said he would remain in post until a new Labour leader is elected.
The Prime Minister made the announcement on Sunday morning, saying he had "agonised" over the decision.
Starmer said he had "given everything" to the role but that it was "time for change".
He said: "I take full responsibility for the results and I've decided to stand down as leader of the Labour Party and as Prime Minister."
The announcement came after Labour suffered heavy losses in the local elections on Thursday, losing the Runcorn and Helsby by-election to Reform UK by just six votes, and losing control of several councils.
